metadata.difficulty_description: Moderate difficulty: 24-year-old woman post-partum (6 weeks after delivery). Postpartum psychosis is the primary mimic. Orofacial dyskinesias and autonomic instability develop gradually. Agent must distinguish anti-NMDAR encephalitis from postpartum psychosis — key differentiators are seizures, EEG, CSF changes, and antibody positivity.

patient.presenting_complaint: Six weeks post-partum woman with worsening agitation, insomnia, confusion, and a witnessed convulsive episode
patient.hpi: A 24-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department by her husband six weeks after the birth of her first child. She had had a normal vaginal delivery at term with no intrapartum complications. In the first two weeks after delivery her husband noted that she appeared more anxious than expected, struggling to sleep even when the baby slept, and seemed preoccupied with fears that something terrible would happen to the baby. The health visitor, attending at week two postpartum, had documented mild postnatal depression and referred her to the community midwife. By week four she had become increasingly agitated, refusing to eat, and had stopped breastfeeding abruptly. She had made several statements to her husband suggesting she believed their baby was 'not her real child.' She was assessed by a community perinatal mental health nurse on day 26 post-delivery who documented probable postpartum psychosis and initiated a referral to the mother and baby unit, but the placement had not yet come through. Over the three days before admission, her husband observed repetitive jaw-clenching and stereotyped hand movements that he could not voluntarily interrupt. On the morning of admission she had a two-minute tonic-clonic seizure for which the husband called emergency services. In the ambulance her heart rate was noted to fluctuate between 140 and 55 bpm. She has no prior psychiatric history and no prior seizure disorder. She is not on any regular medications. No family history of psychiatric disease.

red_herrings.data_point: Six weeks post-partum with psychosis, insomnia, and delusions
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Postpartum psychosis does not cause seizures, orofacial dyskinesias, or autonomic instability. EEG and CSF changes confirm organic aetiology. Anti-NMDAR encephalitis can present post-partum, possibly triggered by immunological changes of pregnancy/delivery.

red_herrings.data_point: Elevated anti-TPO antibodies (186 IU/mL) and family history of Hashimoto thyroiditis
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Anti-TPO elevation is incidental — post-partum thyroiditis risk is elevated, and family history predisposes. However, free T4 is normal (Hashimoto encephalopathy requires thyroid dysfunction). Anti-NMDAR antibodies confirmed at high titre are the correct diagnosis.

CSF shows lymphocytic pleocytosis (not neutrophilic), no organisms, normal glucose. Bacterial meningitis excluded. Blood cultures pending but clinical picture is autoimmune, not infectious. Post-partum leucocytosis is physiological.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis with right ovarian mature teratoma — presenting in post-partum period

differential.key_features: Seizures, orofacial dyskinesias, autonomic instability, EEG encephalopathy, and CSF pleocytosis are NOT features of postpartum psychosis. Anti-NMDAR antibodies confirmed.
Anti-TPO elevated but free T4 normal. Anti-NMDAR antibodies at high titre confirmed. Elevated anti-TPO is incidental given family history and post-partum thyroiditis risk.
MRV normal. No venous thrombosis. Post-partum CVT typically presents differently (progressive headache, focal deficits, not psychiatric).
HSV PCR negative. MRI shows left temporal changes without haemorrhage. Anti-NMDAR confirmed.

optimal_actions.action: MRI brain with MRV to exclude cerebral venous thrombosis (critical post-partum differential)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Left medial temporal FLAIR change; normal MRV — CVT excluded

optimal_actions.action: EEG urgently given seizures and autonomic instability
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Severe encephalopathy; possible left temporal electrographic seizure — anti-seizure therapy urgent

optimal_actions.action: Lumbar puncture — CSF analysis including autoimmune encephalitis antibodies
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Lymphocytic pleocytosis, elevated protein, oligoclonal bands, anti-NMDAR antibodies pending

optimal_actions.action: ECG and continuous cardiac monitoring given autonomic instability
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Alternating tachycardia/bradycardia — autonomic dysregulation; borderline QTc

optimal_actions.action: Recognise elevated anti-TPO as incidental — confirm with free T4 to exclude Hashimoto encephalopathy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Free T4 normal — Hashimoto encephalopathy excluded. Anti-TPO is incidental (family history, post-partum thyroiditis).

optimal_actions.action: Send anti-NMDAR antibodies serum and CSF
Initiate first-line immunotherapy empirically given high suspicion (severity of illness with autonomic instability warrants no further delay)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: IVMP + IVIG first-line; ITU admission for airway and autonomic monitoring
Right ovarian mature teratoma — laparoscopic oophorectomy indicated

critical_actions: MRV mandatory in post-partum encephalopathy to exclude cerebral venous thrombosis
Autonomic instability with tachycardia/bradycardia cycling requires ITU-level monitoring
Elevated anti-TPO in context of positive anti-NMDAR antibodies is incidental — do not diagnose Hashimoto encephalopathy
Do not delay immunotherapy in severe anti-NMDAR encephalitis with autonomic instability and ongoing seizures
Pelvic ultrasound for ovarian teratoma — right oophorectomy required
contraindicated_actions: Treat as postpartum psychosis with antipsychotics alone without investigating for encephalitis
Attribute all findings to Hashimoto encephalopathy based on elevated anti-TPO without checking free thyroid hormones
Omit MRV in post-partum period (CVT must be excluded)
Administer QTc-prolonging antipsychotics without ECG monitoring in autonomic instability
key_reasoning_points: Anti-NMDAR encephalitis can present post-partum and is a critical mimic of postpartum psychosis. Seizures and orofacial dyskinesias never occur in postpartum psychosis and mandate encephalitis workup.
MRV is essential in post-partum encephalopathy — cerebral venous thrombosis is a life-threatening post-partum complication that must be excluded.

Elevated anti-TPO antibodies in a post-partum woman with a family history of thyroid disease are incidental — Hashimoto encephalopathy requires abnormal free thyroid hormones. This is a deliberate moderate-difficulty red herring.
Autonomic instability (cyclic tachycardia/bradycardia, hypertension/hypotension) is a hallmark of anti-NMDAR encephalitis and indicates hypothalamic-brainstem involvement — ITU admission required.
Ovarian teratomas may become clinically apparent or immunologically active post-partum due to peri-partum immune changes. The teratoma may have been asymptomatic throughout pregnancy.

findings.location: Medial temporal lobe (left hippocampus and amygdala)

mri.impression: Normal magnetic resonance venography. No evidence of cerebral venous sinus thrombosis. No acute intracranial abnormality, mass, hemorrhage, or restricted diffusion. Clinical correlation recommended.

background.posterior_dominant_rhythm: Poorly organized theta activity, 6-7 Hz, replacing expected alpha rhythm

findings.morphology: Severe generalised slowing. No discernible alpha activity. Background predominantly 4-5 Hz delta-theta range. Severely disorganised.

Focal rhythmic delta activity over left temporal region (T3, F7) — intermittent bursts of 1-1.5 Hz delta, lasting 20-30 seconds. Possible electrographic seizure morphology in one burst with evolution of frequency and spatial spread.
Possible left temporal electrographic seizure captured. No extreme delta brush. Severe encephalopathic background.

eeg.impression: This is an ABNORMAL EEG due to: 1. Diffuse encephalopathic background. 2. Possible left temporal electrographic seizure with evolving morphology. No extreme delta brush pattern identified. Clinical correlation recommended.

results.title: Anti-NMDAR encephalitis presenting as postpartum psychosis
results.summary: Anti-NMDAR encephalitis can present in the post-partum period mimicking postpartum psychosis. Key distinguishing features: (1) seizures are not a feature of postpartum psychosis — their occurrence mandates encephalitis workup; (2) orofacial dyskinesias are specific to anti-NMDAR encephalitis; (3) autonomic instability (HR/BP fluctuations) is not a feature of postpartum psychosis; (4) EEG encephalopathy and CSF pleocytosis confirm organic aetiology. Ovarian teratomas may become symptomatic post-partum due to immunological changes of pregnancy and delivery.

ct.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No haemorrhage, mass, hydrocephalus, or large-territory infarct.

findings: Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.
No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.
